title: Add marketplace quickstart example app (AWS/GCP) + first-call checklist
author: Wei Chen
description:
This adds a small, runnable example app tailored for AWS/GCP Marketplace buyers to hit the "first successful request" milestone with minimal friction. It includes a guided environment setup flow, explicit entitlement/provisioning prerequisites, and a troubleshooting section for the most common marketplace pitfalls (entitlement propagation delay, org linking mismatch, wrong region, and missing API key scope). The app intentionally mirrors the marketplace onboarding sequence: subscribe -> verify entitlement -> create/link Redwood org -> create API key -> make a streaming request. This is meant to be linked from the marketplace onboarding docs and used by SE/Support as a reproducible baseline during escalations.

What’s included: a Node.js (TypeScript) example app with a minimal UI + CLI runner, a copy/paste .env template, and a "first-call" script that validates required inputs before sending a request. The example defaults to the Hosted API path, but the README calls out how Dedicated/Private customers should obtain base URLs and any org policy differences.

Key behavior: if REDWOOD_MARKETPLACE_PROVIDER is set (aws|gcp), the app prints provider-specific guidance, including where to confirm subscription/entitlement and what to do if the Redwood Console shows "No active entitlement" yet. We don’t call internal entitlement APIs directly from the example (to avoid coupling + creds), but we document the expected signals and link to the Console screens.

Example request used by the app (streaming chat):

curl -N https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood/verified-llama","stream":true,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hello and include a UUID."}]}'

Why now: Marketplace refresh work has highlighted that we lose a meaningful number of buyers between subscription and first token due to unclear prerequisites and entitlement delays (see SUP-4821). This example provides a consistent "known good" path for customers and internal teams.

Out of scope: any changes to entitlement verification endpoints (handled in the core repo) and any billing/metering changes.
